summary: This is a draft for counsel's review, computed from the record with machine-checked lines (investigator lines matched by key words in code; the suspect's lines labeled by a model and checked by code). Borderline suspect-side calls need review. Across 24 key details Brendan Dassey stated or agreed to, investigators introduced 9 first, 4 were already public before the interviews, 1 may trace to an earlier statement with no public transcript, and 10 originated with him in the available record. One detail raised by investigators (a tattoo on her stomach) was never adopted. The three recorded sessions show high interrogator word share (68–88%), hundreds of fact-carrying questions, and repeated use of "we already know," minimization, and "demand truth" tactics.

The suspect volunteered 10 details first in the record: tied up with rope (p. 471), restrained on bed (p. 566), stabbed in stomach (p. 469), strangled unconscious (p. 579), hair cut (p. 584), throat cut (p. 586), shot with .22 rifle (p. 587), RAV4 hidden in salvage yard (p. 459), bedsheets burned (p. 607), bones broken with shovel (p. 637).

Four details were publicly reported before any interview: body burned behind garage (Nov 16, 2005; investigators p. 442, suspect p. 473), license plates removed (Nov 16, 2005; investigators p. 601, suspect p. 602), vehicle key in bedroom (Nov 10, 2005; suspect p. 602), clothes burned (Nov 16, 2005; investigators p. 451, suspect p. 471).

One detail (bleach on jeans from cleaning garage floor) may trace to an earlier statement with no public transcript (Decision and Order p. 7, citing ECF 19-19 at 10–11); it first appears in the transcripts at p. 527.
Investigators raised a tattoo on her stomach (p. 662) but the suspect never stated or agreed to it.

Session dynamics: S1 (Feb 27) 87.5% interrogator words, 306 questions (102 fact-carrying), 6 "we already know" and 9 minimization tactics; S2 (Mar 1) 68.4% interrogator words, 1,154 questions (366 fact-carrying), 36 "we already know" and 16 minimization tactics; S3 (May 13) 73.3% interrogator words, 847 questions (291 fact-carrying), 10 "we already know" and 5 minimization tactics.
limits: The audit covers only the 24 coded key details; it does not assess the full narrative or every statement in the transcripts.
Two sessions (S1b at Two Rivers PD and S1c with Fassbender) have no public transcript; the bleach detail is noted as possibly originating there but cannot be verified from the record.
Origin coding reflects the earliest appearance in the available transcripts; it does not prove independent knowledge or rule out contamination from unrecorded contacts.
The audit does not evaluate voluntariness, reliability, or the legal admissibility of any statement.
